title: Pentagons Are Terrible at One Thing
beats: Hexagons are the bestagons because bees; dismiss 'bees are hexapods' explanation
Bee's engineering problem: wax costs 8 units of honey; maximize honey, minimize wax
Honeycomb conjecture; define tiling as covering a surface with polygons
Enumerate: complex tiles waste wall; only triangle, square, hexagon tile; pentagons leave gaps
Squares and triangles self-divide into lines; hexagon indivisible
Counting 'one..six' reveals hidden hexagons in triangles and irregular tilings
Back to honeycomb; circles waste space, and their packing is a hidden hexagon
Min wall for max area; same reason in bee eyes
Your retina cells are a hexagonal grid too
Saturn's hexagon: unexplained mystery, gas giant so not geology; joke about aliens
Snowflakes: zoom to water molecules preferring hexagons; 12-sided flakes caveat; ice 1h
Graphite and graphene: hexagonal carbon, 100x steel
Second reason: 120-degree three-way joints are most stable per material
Re-look at the tiling as a network of stable joints; basalt, bubbles
If strong, why does pencil write? Strong in-plane, weak between layers
Honeycomb panels for aircraft and rockets
Game boards: squares warp diagonal distance (root 2); hexes equidistant six neighbors
Mock-cult conclusion: hexagons are the bestagons; spread the order

theory: The video is a single claim (hexagons give max area per wall and the most stable joints) re-proven across roughly ten domains, held together by a comic refrain. The pedagogical engine is the counting reveal: after hexagons appear 'hidden' twice, viewers start finding them unprompted, which turns repetition into discovery. Rigor is thin by design; breadth plus a recurring mechanism is what makes it stick.
velocity: Scene builder: 'hidden structure reveal' primitive that highlights six neighbors one by one with a count voiceover
Orchestrator: after two guided reveals, pause and let the learner find the third (ghost hands only on timeout)
Playbook: one-mechanism-many-domains for property-explains-ubiquity topics; anchor each domain back to the same named mechanism
Evals: check learner states the mechanism (min wall/max area, 120-degree joints), not just the slogan
